context: An elderly couple walks in the park
purpose: Teach: 鳴る/さっと/一段と/行き来/ハンカチ/飴/尻尾/足首

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 公園の鐘、夕方に鳴るな。
lines.en: The park bell rings at dusk, doesn't it.
lines.style: Soft, observational opening. Quiet certainty — the statement of someone who has heard this bell many times before. Slow, measured pace. Voice settles like evening itself.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。さっと帰り支度しましょ。
lines.en: Yes. We should start heading back.
lines.style: Gentle agreement with practical care underneath. Warm but not fussy. Slight nod in the voice. Ready to move without rushing him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 冷え込み、一段と厳しいな。
lines.en: The cold's getting sharper, isn't it.
lines.style: Quiet observation delivered with the smallest edge of wry humor. Not complaining — noticing. Eyes crinkling slightly. Matter-of-fact, unbothered.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い夫婦の行き来、公園で増えたわね。
lines.en: There are more young couples coming to the park these days.
lines.style: Soft, watching tone. Gentle observation with a touch of curiosity. She's noticing the world shift, not judging it. Voice carries a small smile.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ハンカチ、ベンチに忘れずに。
lines.en: Don't leave the handkerchief on the bench.
lines.style: Practical reminder delivered with quiet affection. Not fussy — just the voice of someone who knows him. Light, steady concern woven in so naturally it's almost invisible.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 孫に、飴、買って帰りましょう。
lines.en: We should buy some candy for the grandchildren on the way back.
lines.style: Tender anticipation — the thought of the kids already warming her voice. Slightly brighter than before. Gentle, giving. The voice of someone whose affection is easy and genuine.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 隣の犬、尻尾振って、こっち来た。
lines.en: The neighbor's dog came over, wagging its tail.
lines.style: Light, small smile in the voice. A moment of genuine delight breaking through. Warm, present observation. The pace softens — he's watching the dog, not hurrying.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 帰ったら、足首、温めましょう。
lines.en: When we get home, we should warm our ankles by the heater.
lines.style: Closing thought delivered with practical tenderness. Voice softens toward the end — the comfort of routine, of home. Care wrapped in simplicity. Almost to herself, but including him.
